# Fieldbound Asset Specification

**Version:** 1
**Owner:** content-designer
**Generated by:** `scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs`
**Manifest:** `public/assets/assets.manifest.json`

This document is the swap contract for Fieldbound art. The manifest is the only
mapping from a content id to a file, and the loader in
`src/assets/asset-manifest.ts` is the only way the application turns an id into a
URL. Replacing an SVG at its manifest path must not require an engine, controller
or UI edit (CNT-FR-05, CNT-FR-06, VIS-CON-06).

---

## 1. Directory layout

```text
public/assets/
  assets.manifest.json          # generated; the id -> file mapping
  cards/<card-id>.svg           # 32 files
  enemies/<enemy-id>.svg        # 4 files
  fields/field-<element>.svg    # 5 files
```

At build time Vite copies `public/` to the root of `dist/`, so the same files
are served from `<base>assets/...`. No asset is fetched from another origin.

| Kind | Count | Id namespace | Manifest path | Public URL |
|------|-------|--------------|---------------|------------|
| Card | 32 | `card:<card-id>` | `cards/<card-id>.svg` | `<base>assets/cards/<card-id>.svg` |
| Enemy | 4 | `enemy:<enemy-id>` | `enemies/<enemy-id>.svg` | `<base>assets/enemies/<enemy-id>.svg` |
| Field | 5 | `field:<element>` | `fields/field-<element>.svg` | `<base>assets/fields/field-<element>.svg` |

Field ids are exactly `field:ember`, `field:frost`, `field:gale`, `field:stone`
and `field:neutral`. Enemy ids keep the content prefix, so Cinder Warden is
`enemy:enemy-cinder-warden`.

Naming rules:

- ids and file names are lowercase kebab-case, matching the content catalog;
- a field file is `field-<element>.svg`, not `<element>.svg`;
- paths in the manifest are relative, use forward slashes and never start with
  `/`; the loader adds `assets/`.

---

## 2. Manifest schema

The manifest is versioned JSON with a class-wide `spec` block and one entry per
asset. Entries are sorted by id. Entry dimensions, format and safe area mirror
the `spec` block for the entry's kind so a consumer can reserve layout space
without joining two structures (VIS-NFR-02).

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "generatedBy": "scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs",
  "spec": {
    "card": {
      "width": 300,
      "height": 420,
      "format": "svg",
      "safeArea": 24,
      "titleBand": 72,
      "artBox": [240, 200],
      "textBand": 96
    },
    "enemy": { "width": 512, "height": 512, "format": "svg", "safeArea": 32 },
    "field": { "width": 256, "height": 256, "format": "svg", "safeArea": 16 }
  },
  "assets": [
    {
      "id": "card:ember-cinder-jab",
      "kind": "card",
      "element": "ember",
      "name": "Cinder Jab",
      "path": "cards/ember-cinder-jab.svg",
      "width": 300,
      "height": 420,
      "format": "svg",
      "safeArea": 24
    },
    {
      "id": "enemy:enemy-cinder-warden",
      "kind": "enemy",
      "element": "ember",
      "name": "Cinder Warden",
      "path": "enemies/enemy-cinder-warden.svg",
      "width": 512,
      "height": 512,
      "format": "svg",
      "safeArea": 32
    },
    {
      "id": "field:ember",
      "kind": "field",
      "element": "ember",
      "name": "Ember Field",
      "path": "fields/field-ember.svg",
      "width": 256,
      "height": 256,
      "format": "svg",
      "safeArea": 16
    }
  ]
}
```

`name` is the display name used for alt text and the labelled fallback. It is
copied from the card or enemy catalog, or is `<Element> Field` for fields.

---

## 3. Dimensions and safe areas

| Kind | Canvas | Safe area | Additional layout metadata |
|------|--------|-----------|----------------------------|
| Card | **300 x 420** | **24 px** inset on all sides | `titleBand: 72` (top), `artBox: [240, 200]` at x 30, y 96, `textBand: 96` (bottom) |
| Enemy | **512 x 512** | **32 px** inset on all sides | bottom 96 px is a decorative band; the name baseline sits above it at y 392 |
| Field | **256 x 256** | **16 px** inset on all sides | glyph centred at y 112, label baseline at y 216 |

Rules:

- text, badges and the geometric glyph stay inside the safe area;
- background fills, the outer frame and decorative bands may extend outside it;
- the card art box is exactly 240 x 200, so the board can reserve the art area
  before the SVG decodes and avoid layout shift;
- a replacement keeps the same canvas size. If a whole class changes size, bump
  `version` in the manifest and update both `spec` and this table in the same
  change.

---

## 4. Element palette

The generator and `docs/ASSET-SPEC.md` share these values. Do not duplicate hex
values in components; a replacement SVG may use the palette but is not required
to.

| Element | Base (background) | Accent (frame/glyph) | Ink (text) | Shade (badge text/bands) |
|---------|-------------------|----------------------|------------|--------------------------|
| Ember | `#7f1d1d` warm red | `#f59e0b` amber | `#fff7ed` | `#450a0a` |
| Frost | `#1e3a8a` deep blue | `#a5f3fc` pale cyan | `#eff6ff` | `#172554` |
| Gale | `#115e59` teal green | `#a7f3d0` light mint | `#ecfdf5` | `#042f2e` |
| Stone | `#5b4636` brown | `#d6b98c` sand | `#fdf6e3` | `#2f241b` |
| Neutral | `#374151` grey | `#e5e7eb` off-white | `#f9fafb` | `#111827` |

The placeholder text uses the generic `sans-serif` family. No web font is
loaded, no image is fetched and no audio file is referenced (VIS-CON-06).

---

## 5. Placeholder content

Each generated SVG carries, as applicable:

- the element palette and a plain frame;
- a geometric glyph (an element mark for enemies and fields, a card-type mark
  for cards);
- the card name, cost badge, a data-derived effect summary and an
  `<element> / <type>` footer;
- the enemy name, element, health badge and `HP` label;
- the field name and a `FIELD` caption;
- an SVG `<title>` for assistive technology and the generated banner comment.

The effect summary is presentation text derived from the effect descriptors in
`cards.json`. It is not a rule: the engine remains the only interpreter of
damage, defense, draw, energy, status and field changes (VIS-CON-08).

---

## 6. Loader contract

```ts
import { resolveAsset } from './assets/asset-manifest';

const src = resolveAsset(`card:${card.id}`, import.meta.env.BASE_URL);
```

- `resolveAsset(id, baseUrl)` returns `<normalized base>assets/<manifest path>`
  or `undefined` for an unknown id. It never throws.
- The loader does not read `import.meta.env`, `window`, `document` or storage;
  the caller supplies the base once.
- `normalizeBase` strips trailing slashes and adds exactly one, so `/`,
  `/Card-Game-Project/` and `/Card-Game-Project` all produce a single slash
  between the base and `assets/`.
- A leading-slash path is never resolved with `new URL(..., base)`, because that
  would escape a GitHub Pages project subpath (VIS-CON-02).
- Components render a labelled text fallback when the result is `undefined` or
  the image fails to load. Alt text comes from the manifest `name` or the content
  definition, never from the file path.
- Components must not import an SVG through Vite. Every image goes through
  `resolveAsset`, which is what keeps replacement code-free.

---

## 7. Replacing an SVG

1. Find the entry in `public/assets/assets.manifest.json` by id (for example
   `card:ember-cinder-jab`).
2. Read its `path`, `width`, `height` and `safeArea`.
3. Replace the file at exactly that path (`public/assets/cards/ember-cinder-jab.svg`)
   with an SVG of the same canvas size.
4. Keep the file name unchanged. The manifest is the mapping; do not reinterpret
   the naming convention.
5. Do not run `node scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs` afterwards for that
   asset: regeneration rewrites every placeholder and overwrites the
   replacement. A whole-set regeneration replaces all committed art.
6. Run `npm test -- src/assets/asset-manifest.test.ts` and
   `node scripts/check-budget.mjs`.
7. Commit the replaced SVG. No engine, controller or UI edit is needed.

The manifest test treats a missing file, a missing entry, an extra entry, a
duplicate id or path, an absolute or backslash path, a wrong canvas size and an
out-of-date generator output as failures.

---

## 8. Adding or removing content

The asset set is derived from the catalogs, so content and art change together:

1. Add or remove the card or enemy in `src/content/cards.json` or
   `src/content/enemies.json`, or change a field element list.
2. Run `node scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs`. This writes one SVG per
   asset, removes stale SVGs whose names are no longer in the manifest, and
   rewrites `public/assets/assets.manifest.json`.
3. Run `npm test -- src/assets/asset-manifest.test.ts` and
   `npm test -- src/content/content.test.ts`.
4. Commit the catalog, the manifest, every changed SVG and any update to this
   document together.

---

## 9. Determinism

`scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs`:

- sorts manifest entries by id with a plain code-unit comparison;
- uses integer coordinates, fixed attribute order and LF endings;
- embeds no timestamp, random value, build counter, locale-dependent formatting
  or absolute path;
- writes stable two-space JSON with a trailing newline;
- supports `--check`, which compares the expected bytes with the files on disk
  and exits non-zero on any missing, extra or different file without writing.

Two consecutive runs therefore produce byte-identical SVGs and manifest. The
manifest test runs `--check` twice to enforce that guarantee.

---

## 10. Validation

```bash
node scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs
node scripts/generate-placeholder-assets.mjs --check
npm test -- src/assets/asset-manifest.test.ts
npm run typecheck
```

Expected result: 41 SVGs (32 cards, 4 enemies, 5 fields), one manifest with 41
entries, and `--check` reporting that the output is byte-identical.
